planting.note: Plant seedlings in spring in rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade; Catimor Coffee is frost-tender and best grown as a container plant brought indoors for winter outside zones 10-11.

directions: Bred in Portugal in the 1950s by crossing the dwarf Caturra with the naturally rust-resistant Hybrido de Timor, Catimor introduced leaf rust resistance into commercial Arabica production for the first time and has since become one of the most widely planted cultivars across Central America, South Asia, and parts of Africa. Its compact, dwarf habit and early, heavy bearing make it attractive for smallholders and high-density plantings, though cup quality is generally considered a step below heirloom lines like Bourbon or Typica unless carefully processed. Give it the same warm, filtered-shade conditions and consistently moist, well-drained soil that other Arabicas need, and expect the first harvest within three years of transplanting.
sources: Centro de Investigação das Ferrugens do Cafeeiro (CIFC), Portugal
Purdue University Center for New Crops and Plants Products

planting.note: Plant seedlings in spring in rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade; Sarchimor Coffee is frost-tender and best grown as a container plant brought indoors for winter outside zones 10-11.

directions: Developed by crossing the dwarf Villa Sarchi with the rust-resistant Hybrido de Timor, Sarchimor carries the same disease resistance as Catimor but from a different dwarf parent, and it has become the foundational lineage behind many newer rust-resistant varieties such as Marsellesa, Costa Rica 95, and IHCAFE90. Growers and roasters generally regard Sarchimor-derived selections as capable of better cup quality than straight Catimor lines when grown at good elevation and carefully processed. It forms a somewhat taller, more open shrub than Catimor and bears reliably once established. Provide the dappled shade, steady moisture, and rich, well-drained acidic soil favored by other highland Arabicas.
sources: CATIE (Centro Agronómico Tropical de Investigación y Enseñanza)
Purdue University Center for New Crops and Plants Products

planting.note: Plant seedlings in spring in rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade; Castillo Coffee is frost-tender and best grown as a container plant brought indoors for winter outside zones 10-11.

directions: Released in 2005 by Colombia's Cenicáfe research center, Castillo was bred to replace the aging, increasingly rust-susceptible Colombia variety while preserving comparable cup quality, and it is now the dominant cultivar on Colombian farms. It combines solid resistance to coffee leaf rust with a compact, productive habit suited to the country's steep, densely planted hillside farms. Growers value its dependable yields and disease tolerance, while roasters generally find its cup quality good, if slightly more variable regionally than older heirloom Colombian selections. Grow it as for other Arabicas, in filtered shade with rich, moist, well-drained soil.
sources: Cenicáfe (Centro Nacional de Investigaciones de Café), Colombia
Federación Nacional de Cafeteros de Colombia

planting.note: Plant seedlings in spring in rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade; Ruiru 11 Coffee is frost-tender and best grown as a container plant brought indoors for winter outside zones 10-11.

directions: Released in 1985 by Kenya's Coffee Research Foundation, Ruiru 11 was the first Arabica cultivar bred with combined resistance to both coffee berry disease and leaf rust, the two most destructive coffee diseases in East Africa, and its dwarf, highly compact habit allows far denser planting than traditional Kenyan selections like SL28. It is an F1 composite hybrid, so seed must be sourced from the breeding program rather than saved from open-pollinated trees. Cup quality is respectable but historically ranked below the legendary SL28 and SL34, a gap that later prompted the breeding of the successor cultivar Batian. Grow it in filtered shade with rich, well-drained soil and expect early, heavy bearing.
sources: Purdue University Center for New Crops and Plants Products

planting.note: Plant seedlings in spring in rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade; Batian Coffee is frost-tender and best grown as a container plant brought indoors for winter outside zones 10-11.

directions: Released in 2010 by Kenya's Coffee Research Institute as the successor to Ruiru 11, Batian retains resistance to both coffee berry disease and leaf rust but was specifically selected to close the cup-quality gap with heirloom Kenyan cultivars such as SL28 and SL34. It grows into a taller, more open shrub than the very compact Ruiru 11 and comes into bearing faster, giving growers an earlier return on establishment costs. Kenyan producers value it as a disease-resistant option that still produces the bright, complex cup quality Kenyan coffee is known for. Cultivate it under the same filtered shade and rich, well-drained acidic soil conditions as other Arabica selections.

planting.note: Plant seedlings in spring in rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade; Marsellesa Coffee is frost-tender and best grown as a container plant brought indoors for winter outside zones 10-11.

directions: Selected by the French agricultural research center CIRAD from Sarchimor lineage, Marsellesa is a pure-line, non-hybrid rust-resistant cultivar that has been widely distributed across Nicaragua, Honduras, and other Central American coffee regions as a more affordable, seed-saveable alternative to F1 hybrids. Because it breeds true from seed, smallholders can maintain their own planting stock without repurchasing hybrid seed each generation, a significant practical advantage over cultivars like Ruiru 11 or Centroamericano. Cup quality is generally considered good for a rust-resistant selection when grown at adequate elevation. Provide the same filtered shade, steady moisture, and rich acidic soil that other Sarchimor-derived cultivars need.
sources: CIRAD (Centre de coopération internationale en recherche agronomique pour le développement)

planting.note: Plant seedlings in spring in rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade; Starmaya Coffee is frost-tender and best grown as a container plant brought indoors for winter outside zones 10-11.

directions: Bred jointly by CIRAD and ECOM Sustainable Management Services and released around 2018, Starmaya was the first F1 Arabica hybrid that could be propagated economically by seed rather than requiring costly embryo-culture or clonal cutting propagation, making the vigor and yield benefits of F1 hybrids accessible to smallholders for the first time. It combines a dwarf, compact growth habit with strong vigor, reliable production, and good cup quality reported by early adopters in Nicaragua and Mexico. Because it is still a hybrid, seed should be sourced from certified programs to maintain its traits. Grow it under filtered shade in rich, well-drained soil like other Arabica selections.
sources: CIRAD (Centre de coopération internationale en recherche agronomique pour le développement)

planting.note: Plant seedlings in spring in rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade; Centroamericano Coffee is frost-tender and best grown as a container plant brought indoors for winter outside zones 10-11.

directions: Developed through a regional breeding collaboration led by World Coffee Research and PROMECAFE, Centroamericano is an F1 hybrid bred specifically for Central American smallholders, combining leaf rust resistance with yields substantially higher than long-standing regional standards like Caturra and Catuai. As an F1 hybrid its full vigor and yield benefits are only expressed in the first hybrid generation, so growers must obtain fresh hybrid seed from licensed nurseries rather than save their own. Field trials across the region have reported strong performance under real smallholder conditions rather than just experiment-station settings. Cultivate it under filtered shade with rich, moist, well-drained soil as with other Arabica cultivars.
sources: PROMECAFE (Programa Cooperativo Regional para el Desarrollo Tecnológico y Modernización de la Caficultura)

planting.note: Plant seedlings in spring in rich, moist, well-drained soil in partial shade; ICS 1 Cacao is a frost-tender tropical tree realistic outdoors only in zones 10-11.

directions: Selected in Trinidad in the early twentieth century by the breeding program at the Imperial College of Tropical Agriculture, ICS 1 belongs to the historic 'Imperial College Selection' series of Trinitario-type clones prized for excellent chocolate flavor and still maintained in cacao germplasm collections worldwide. It has been used both as a direct planting material valued by fine-flavor chocolate makers and as parent stock in countless later breeding programs seeking to combine good flavor with improved vigor or disease resistance. Growth habit is moderately vigorous and upright, similar to other Trinitario selections. Grow it under the same filtered shade and rich, moist soil conditions favored by heirloom cacao types.
sources: Cocoa Research Centre, University of the West Indies, Trinidad

planting.note: Plant seedlings in spring in rich, moist, well-drained soil in partial shade; SCA 6 Cacao is a frost-tender tropical tree realistic outdoors only in zones 10-11.

directions: Collected in Peru in the early twentieth century as one of the 'Scavina' upper Amazon Forastero-type clones, SCA 6 is significant chiefly as one of the two parent clones, alongside IMC 67, used to breed the high-yield, disease-resistant CCN-51 hybrid that transformed Ecuadorian cacao production. On its own it contributes strong resistance to witches'-broom disease and notably vigorous, fast growth compared to heirloom Criollo or Trinitario types. Its beans are considered workmanlike bulk cacao rather than fine flavor. Grow it in the same warm, humid, partially shaded conditions as other cacao selections, expecting rapid early growth.
sources: Cocoa Research Centre, University of the West Indies, Trinidad

planting.note: Plant seedlings in spring in rich, moist, well-drained soil in partial shade; EET 400 Cacao is a frost-tender tropical tree realistic outdoors only in zones 11-12.

directions: Bred by Ecuador's INIAP (Instituto Nacional de Investigaciones Agropecuarias) at its Pichilingue Experiment Station, EET 400 was selected from Nacional-type parentage specifically to combine the prized floral 'Arriba' fine-flavor aroma with better yield and disease tolerance than unimproved heirloom Nacional trees. It is grown commercially in Ecuador alongside high-yield hybrids like CCN-51 by producers who want to retain access to fine-flavor cacao price premiums rather than switch entirely to bulk cacao. Growth habit and vigor fall between the very heavy-bearing CCN-51 and the more delicate heirloom Nacional. Cultivate it with the same filtered shade and rich, well-drained soil other Nacional-lineage cacao needs.
sources: INIAP (Instituto Nacional de Investigaciones Agropecuarias), Ecuador

planting.note: Plant seedlings in spring in rich, moist, well-drained soil in partial shade; Amelonado Cacao is a frost-tender tropical tree realistic outdoors only in zones 10-11.

directions: The classic lower-Amazon Forastero-type variety introduced to West Africa in the nineteenth century, Amelonado remains the genetic backbone of cacao production in Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire, the world's two largest cacao-producing countries. It takes its name from its smooth, rounded, melon-shaped pods, distinct from the warty, ridged pods of Criollo. Genetically narrow and largely self-compatible, it produces dependable but modest harvests of solid bulk cacao rather than the fine-flavor beans associated with Criollo or Nacional, and it has served as the foundation for most West African cacao breeding programs. Grow it under filtered shade in rich, moist, well-drained soil like other heirloom cacao types.

common_name: Fuding Dabaicha Tea (Fuding Da Bai Cha)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in spring in acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun; Fuding Dabaicha Tea (Fuding Da Bai Cha) is best suited to USDA zones 8-10.

directions: Originating in Fuding, Fujian Province, China, Fuding Dabaicha ('Fuding Large White Tea') is the primary cultivar behind China's most prized white teas, including Silver Needle and White Peony, thanks to unusually large, plump, downy silver-tipped buds that give white tea its signature fuzzy appearance and delicate sweetness. It is also processed into green tea in the same region. Vigorous and productive compared to many fine Chinese cultivars, it responds well to careful hand plucking of only the youngest bud and adjacent leaf for top-grade white tea, with coarser plucking used for green tea production. Grow it with the same acidic, humus-rich soil and partial shade favored by other tea cultivars.
sources: Tea Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in spring in acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun; Longjing 43 Tea is best suited to USDA zones 8-10.

directions: Bred by the Tea Research Institute of the Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences near Hangzhou and released in the 1980s, Longjing 43 was selected specifically to produce the classic flat, jade-green, pan-fired Longjing (Dragon Well) tea for which the region is famous. Its standout trait is exceptionally early spring budbreak, giving growers a premium early-season harvest advantage over older Longjing-type bushes, along with a delicate, sweet, faintly chestnut-like flavor. Because of its importance to a protected-origin product, authentic Longjing tea from this cultivar commands strong prices in the Chinese domestic market. Grow it in the same acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil as other tea cultivars, harvesting the earliest spring flush by hand for top grade.
sources: Tea Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in spring in acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun; Yutakamidori Tea is best suited to USDA zones 8-10.

directions: Developed in Japan and now the dominant tea cultivar in Kagoshima Prefecture, second nationally only to Yabukita, Yutakamidori is distinguished by notably late budbreak, a trait that helps the tender new growth escape the late spring frosts that can damage earlier-budding cultivars. Its leaves yield a rich, full-bodied, slightly sweeter sencha than Yabukita, making it a popular complement grown alongside Yabukita to spread out harvest timing and add flavor diversity to blended green teas. It tolerates the warmer growing conditions of southern Japan's Kagoshima region well. Cultivate it with the same acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil and partial shade as other tea cultivars, hand-plucking young flushes for the best quality.
sources: National Agriculture and Food Research Organization (NARO), Japan

directions: Plant rooted cuttings in spring in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade, training the vine up a sturdy support post. Also known locally as Sarawak pepper, Kuching is the leading cultivar grown across Sarawak, Malaysia, prized internationally for producing unusually large, dense berry clusters that give Sarawak black and white pepper their reputation for superior pungency, aroma, and heavier grain weight than pepper from many other origins. It is a moderately vigorous vine that rewards the intensive fertilization typical of Malaysian pepper gardens with heavy, consistent yields. Maintain warmth above 60°F with high humidity and consistent soil moisture, and expect the vine to reach full production within a few years of establishment.

Plant rooted cuttings in spring in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade, allowing the vine to climb a living or artificial support post. Named for its village of origin in Kerala, India, Uthirankotta is a traditional landrace selection valued by South Indian growers for consistently high yields and better tolerance of common pepper diseases than many older local types, along with good adaptability across the varied soils of the Western Ghats pepper belt. Its medium-length spikes carry a dense set of berries that mature reliably under the humid, filtered-shade conditions of traditional homestead pepper gardens. Keep the root zone evenly moist and mulched, and provide a living standard such as areca palm for the vine to climb.

Plant rooted cuttings in spring in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade, training the vine onto a sturdy support. Kalluvally is another traditional Western Ghats landrace from Kerala, India, distinguished by unusually long spikes and heavier-than-average berry clusters that make it a favorite among smallholders seeking better yields without switching to formally bred hybrids. It performs particularly well on the lateritic soils common across its home region and is traditionally intercropped with areca palm or coconut, which double as its living climbing support. Provide consistent moisture, warmth above 60°F, and dappled shade, and expect steady production once the vine matures.

Plant rooted cuttings in spring in moist, fertile, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade, training the vine up a sturdy living or artificial support post. Released by the Pepper Research Station in Panniyur, Kerala, India as a successor to the original Panniyur-1 hybrid, Panniyur-2 was bred specifically for improved tolerance to Phytophthora foot rot, the most economically damaging disease of cultivated black pepper, while retaining good yield potential. It is commonly recommended for growing sites with higher disease pressure where Panniyur-1 alone proves too vulnerable. Maintain consistent humidity, warmth above 60°F, and even soil moisture without waterlogging, and expect bearing to begin three to four years after planting.
